device.note: software GL: judge order and layout, not cadence

observed: Dietary preferences popped by a short (220 px) swipe. The chevron bubble in the frames is Android's system back gesture (3-button/gesture navigation owns the left edge), not the app's edge tracking. The app's edge pan was not shown by this input: the swipe started inside the system gesture zone. Flutter's VelocityTracker counts the pointer-down event as a sample, M2 measures velocity over the moves only, and `input swipe` injects few, coarse events (a 'fling' from three samples), so a short swipe can read as a fast one; real fingers are unaffected. See edgecancel2 for the app-tracked short drag, which springs back.
frames: extracted at the encoder's real rate (screenrecord emits on change); strip labels give ms from the first frame
black_frames: none (the cold-launch splash in slow.mp4 is Android's, before the app)
